name: copula_dependence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Standard correlation measures linear dependence but misses tail dependence — the tendency for stocks to move together during extreme events (crashes, rallies) differently than during normal periods. A Clayton copula captures lower tail dependence (crash co-movements) while a Gumbel copula captures upper tail dependence. By fitting a bivariate copula to rolling 120-bar returns of a stock pair and monitoring the conditional probability of stock B's extreme move given stock A's extreme move, we can identify when tail dependence is abnormally high (expect contagion) or abnormally low (divergence opportunity). The inefficiency exists because copula modeling requires advanced probability theory beyond most market participants.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs (same sector, high normal-time correlation > 0.6)
stock_filter: Both members: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; rolling correlation(60d daily returns) > 0.6

indicators.name: U_A
indicators.params: empirical_cdf(Return_A, window=120) — uniform marginal for stock A

indicators.name: U_B
indicators.params: empirical_cdf(Return_B, window=120) — uniform marginal for stock B

indicators.name: Copula_Theta
indicators.params: MLE estimate of Clayton copula parameter theta on (U_A, U_B), window=120

indicators.name: Cond_Prob
indicators.params: P(U_B < 0.10 | U_A < 0.10) from fitted copula — conditional crash probability

conditions: Stock A has U_A < 0.10 (extreme negative return for A)
Stock B has U_B > 0.30 (B has NOT crashed despite A crashing)
Cond_Prob > 0.40 (historically, when A crashes, B usually follows — but hasn't yet)
This divergence is unusual: Lower_Tail_Dep is in top quartile (Tail_Dep_Pctile > 0.75) historically, meaning the pair should move together in tails
long.confirmation: LONG stock A (buying the crashed leader expecting bounce) OR SHORT stock B (expecting contagion selloff). Direction determined by Cond_Prob direction

conditions: Stock A has U_A > 0.90 (extreme positive return for A)
Stock B has U_B < 0.70 (B has NOT rallied despite A rallying)
Tail dependence is historically high for this pair
short.confirmation: B starts catching up: ROC(B_close, 3) > 0 and moving toward A's direction

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation of divergence

exit.target: U_A and U_B converge to within 20 percentile points of each other (tail dependence resolves)
exit.stop_loss: Divergence widens: abs(U_A - U_B) > 0.70 (pair has fully decoupled)
exit.signal_exit: Copula_Theta drops below 0.5 (tail dependence weakening fundamentally)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L on the divergent stock; or ₹50K on each leg if trading both sides

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during genuine crisis (VIX > 25), all stocks crash together (correlation → 1), making copula-based differentiation meaningless
filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:15 (need 120 bars for copula fitting) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Both stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy trades tail events specifically
filters.event_filter: Skip pair if either stock has earnings (divergence may be fundamental, not transient)
other_filters: Copula fit must have sufficient goodness-of-fit (AIC of Clayton < AIC of independence copula)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — copula modeling is graduate-level probability theory; very few retail or even institutional traders implement real-time copula-based signals at 1-min frequency

weaknesses: Clayton copula MLE on 120 bivariate observations is statistically weak — the theta estimate has high variance, and 120 observations of (U_A, U_B) provide very few joint tail events for reliable tail dependence estimation
The strategy requires U_A < 0.10, which happens only ~12 times per 120-bar window by construction — signal frequency is extremely low (perhaps 1-2 per day across all pairs)

Choosing Clayton copula assumes lower tail dependence is the relevant structure — this may not hold for all stock pairs; some pairs may exhibit upper tail dependence (Gumbel) or symmetric (Frank) dependence instead
prior_art: Nelsen (2006) 'An Introduction to Copulas'; Patton (2006) on copulas for financial time series; copula-based pairs trading in Liew & Wu (2013); tail dependence in Ang & Chen (2002)
notes: Consider using a time-varying copula (e.g., DCC-copula) to capture evolving dependence structure. The copulalib or pyvinecopulib Python libraries provide efficient copula fitting. Pre-screen pairs daily and maintain a watchlist of 5-8 high-tail-dependence pairs.
